# Calibration and comparison limits

Rubric1.0.0 retains all nine user-specified weights. No empirical finding required reweighting. Scores measure the accessible reconstruction chain, including specifically cited accessible supplements, rather than institutional reputation, document length or OMB approval. Scores were reviewed by one analyst; no inter-rater reliability claim is made. One- or two-point differences should not be interpreted as meaningful superiority.

The calibration re-examined BLS SOII, BLS NCS, EBSA settlement, OSHA extinguishers and process safety, FCC IPCS, TSA aircraft operators and flight training, and the direct Coast Guard/CMMC challengers against the same anchors. Full reproducibility requires more than multiplying an asserted total; source provenance and assumptions remain separate dimensions. Conversely, an unexplained federal budget should not invalidate correctly exposed respondent arithmetic. No score changes were necessary. BLS SOII's ECEC dollar32.91 was verified against the September2023 release; its statement mislabels the reference period as December2023. This resolved an evidence question without removing the documented citation defect.

| Sensitivity | Result | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Original100-point rubric | BLS SOII83; EBSA settlement82; OSHA process safety80. TSA mean67.4, range50–76. | Observed cases, not a population ranking. |
| Remove Item13 and14, rescale remaining80points | BLS SOII85.0; BLS NCS83.75; OSHA extinguishers81.25. TSA mean68.375. | The broad non-uniqueness conclusion is not caused solely by favorable cost zeros. This is a sensitivity view, not a replacement rubric. |
| Item12 composite, first four dimensions, max60 | BLS SOII and NCS53; TSA flight training52; CMMC51. TSA mean46.2. | TSA is close to the strongest observed Item12 methods; it is not uniformly weak. |
| High/very-high complexity and high TSA relevance | OSHA process safety80, extinguishers78, benzene77, Coast Guard security77, FCC IPCS76, EPA chemical reporting76; TSA best76. | Close comparators retain useful counterevidence after simple statistical and benefit cases are set aside. Differences are descriptive, not complexity-adjusted causal effects. |
| Length | SEC ADV-E has a compact reproducible model; EBSA settlement is concise; numerous extensive statements contain inconsistent totals or unsupported coefficients. | No automatic points for pages, tables or narrative detail. |

Zero costs can be legitimate and receive full credit. They are not exemplars of nonzero capital estimation. Federal incremental-cost exclusions and budget allocations are assessed on their stated scope and evidence, not on the magnitude of the total. A new collection may justify a zero prior inventory but still needs a gross/new change bridge; lack of a previous collection is not itself a weakness.

Complexity categories are qualitative: low means a few homogeneous tasks, medium means multiple activities or paths, high means substantial segmentation or cost structure, and very high means extensive regulatory or calibrated models. Original labels are retained; moderate was normalized to medium. TSA relevance direct/high was normalized to high; adjacent to medium; method transfer to technique. This metadata harmonization changes no scores.

Sensitivity records: data/score-sensitivity.csv. Agency means and dispersion: data/agency-summary.csv. Most agencies have too few heterogeneous purposive observations to establish agency-wide quality or consistency. Even TSA's ten observations are not a random or matched sample. Findings should be reported by method and collection, with agency summaries explicitly descriptive.

# Rubric v1.0.0
Weights unchanged from the user mission. This measures observable public reconstruction quality, not all internal agency analysis or OMB approval quality.
|Dimension|Max|Full-credit standard|
|---|---:|---|
|Calculation reproducibility|20|Population, responses, activities, frequency, hours, units, annualization and rounding allow independent total reconstruction.|
|Source provenance and currency|15|Material inputs identify authority, dataset/table/series, occupation, geography, dates and transformations; aging input justified.|
|Burden structure and segmentation|15|Meaningful variation captured without rewarding gratuitous complexity.|
|Labor compensation|10|Occupation choice, wages, vintage, fringe/overhead bases and transformations are transparent and defensible.|
|Item 13|10|Applicable capital/O&M/purchased costs, life and annualization reconstruct; justified zero eligible for full credit.|
|Item 14|10|Incremental federal workload, grades/occupations, compensation, contracts and systems reconstruct or defensible zero.|
|Item 15|10|Old total to input/requirement change to reason to classification to quantified effect to new total.|
|Validation and uncertainty|5|Material assumptions supported by administrative evidence, testing, consultation or justified ranges; uncertainty proportionate.|
|Cross-item consistency|5|Narrative, tables, package totals and prior baseline reconcile with explained tolerances.|

Score anchors: 0=no usable support; approximately 25%=bare asserted total; 50%=partly reconstructable with material gaps; 75%=mostly reconstructable with bounded gaps; 100%=independent reconstruction supported. Integer scores require dimension-specific rationale and source locators. Missing/inaccessible evidence means review incomplete, not automatically a zero. Confirmed omission in a retrieved complete document can lose points.
Do not punish a legitimate zero or irrelevant segmentation. Full marks require the reason to be explicit and consistent with collection scope. Do not require sensitivity analysis for simple collections; credible validation can earn full validation marks. Store document thoroughness separately (brief/moderate/extensive), plus complexity and TSA relevance.
Record model arithmetic checks as pass, fail, rounding, or not_tested. A reported equation is not a performed check. Record source retrieval depth separately from scoring.
Revision history: 2026-09-09 v1.0.0: adopts user weights and provides operational scoring anchors; no empirical reweighting.

Freeze note,2026-09-09: rubric1.0.0 is the final Mission1 scoring rubric. All73 reviews have nine dimension scores and rationale; methodology/calibration.md records the final anchor review and sensitivity analysis. No material revision or weight change occurred. Scores remain bounded single-analyst assessments, not a validated agency performance index.
